> 道生之，德畜之，物形之，勢成之.

Chapter 50 was about one person protecting his life: don't pile it up.

Chapter 51 lifts the gaze: the thing that produces and nourishes everything — how does it nourish?

The answer is in two characters almost nobody looks at closely.

## 亭 is a shelter with no walls

亭: 民所安定也 — the place where people settle and are steady. Its form is a small structure with a roof and no walls: somewhere to stop, not somewhere to be enclosed.

毒: 厚也 — to make thick. Here, to let the plant grow thick.

So 亭之毒之 is not "bring it to maturity." It is: give it a roof to pause under, then let it thicken on its own.

## 道生之，德畜之

The Dao produces; 德 stores and feeds.

生 is 出 — bringing forth. 畜 is to accumulate, to keep, to feed — the same 蓄 that chapter 50 warned against when a person does it to himself.

The distinction: 德 accumulates on behalf of the thing, not for itself. Chapter 50's 生生之厚 was a person piling up for his own continuation; 德畜之 has no self at the center of the pile.

## 物形之，勢成之

Form comes from 物; completion comes from 勢.

Two different operations: 形 is the shape the material takes; 成 is what the situation allows it to become.

Which is why one thing can have a fixed form and never complete: form is given by the material, completion by the momentum around it.

## 莫之命而常自然

> 道之尊，德之貴，夫莫之命而常自然.

Nothing commands it, and it is always so of itself.

The honoring of 道 and 德 is not an ordinance. Nobody issued it. It is 常自然 — invariant and self-so. Which is the same 自然 as chapter 25's 道法自然: no higher authority.

## 生而不有，為而不恃，長而不宰

Produce and do not own; act and do not lean on it; let grow and do not 宰.

## 宰 is a servant in a house

宰: 罪人在屋下執事者 — literally, one who works under a roof, an officer inside the house.

The character's history is precise: it names someone who has entered the house and taken up the duties inside it.

So 長而不宰 is not "don't supervise." It is: do not go into that house and take up the post. The thing grows on its own; entering the house means administering its growth, and administration replaces growth with management.

That is why the three clauses are ordered this way: 有 is claiming, 恃 is leaning, 宰 is entering. Each is a deeper degree of the same move.

## 是謂玄德

This is called 玄德 — the dark 德.

玄 is not "mysterious" as a mood. It is the depth of a color: dark, not visible from outside. The 德 that does not show because it never entered the house.

## Why this chapter follows 50

50 said: don't build the layer that can be breached.
51 says: this is also how the source operates. It produces, shelters, thickens — and stays out of the house.

The instruction and the ground, adjacent, so that the instruction does not look like a personal austerity project.

## A test

Take something you have made that is now growing — a team, a piece of writing, a habit. Ask whether you have entered the house: whether the growth now requires your administration. That is 宰, and it is usually invisible from inside.
